gain.definition: A gain is the act of getting something.

gallery.definition: A gallery is a place where art is displayed.
gallery.sentence: Let's go to the gallery to check out the new paintings.

game.definition: A game is something that people do to have fun.

gap.definition: A gap is a difference in the level of two groups.
gap.sentence: The money is to help bridge the gap between rich schools and poor schools.

garden.definition: If you garden, you work in a garden, especially your own garden around your house.

gas.definition: A gas is a substance, such as air, that is not liquid or solid.
gas.sentence: The sun is a giant ball of gas.

gate.definition: A gate is like a door in a fence. It opens to let people go through the fence.
gate.sentence: Please open the gate for me; my hands are full.

gather.definition: If people or things gather, they come together.
gather.sentence: This trip was a kept secret, I gather , until yesterday.

gaze.definition: When someone gazes at someone, they stare at that person for a long time.

gear.definition: Gear is clothing and other equipment, especially in sports.
gear.sentence: Hurry up and get your gear on. The game's about to start.

gender.definition: Gender is a way of grouping nouns in some languages, for example: masculine, feminine & neuter.
gender.sentence: In French, the gender affects everything from the choice of le or la to the adjective endings.

general.definition: Usual; about most things. An idea is a general idea if it's about many things or about most things, not just about one specific thing.
general.sentence: First I will talk about general problems of farming, and then I will talk about the specific problems of wheat farming.

generally.sentence: Generally, men find it easier to lose weight than women.

generate.definition: If you generate something, you create it.
generate.sentence: On the hottest summer days, we are unable to generate enough electricity.

generation.definition: A generation, is all the people or things of about the same age.
generation.sentence: My father belonged to a generation of travellers who saw the world before there was a McDonalds on every corner.

genetic.definition: Something genetic relates to genetics or genes.

gentle.definition: A gentle person is kind and careful not to cause damage, pain, or surprise.
gentle.sentence: That bear is a monster, not at all a gentle giant.

gentleman.definition: A gentleman is a man that treats other nicely, or a man of higher class.

gently.definition: If you do something gently, you do it in a gentle way.
gently.sentence: Micheal kissed Kate gently on the cheek.

genuine.definition: If something is genuine, it is what is says it is and not something else; it is not fake.
genuine.sentence: I have a genuine copy of the famous book.

gesture.definition: A hand sign for friendly communication.

get.sentence: Get your results the next day.

giant.definition: A giant is a very big man or woman, often in fairy tales.
giant.sentence: Jack climbed the beanstalk and found a land ruled by a giant.

gift.definition: A gift is something given to another person voluntarily.
gift.sentence: She has a gift for singing.

girl.definition: A girl is a female child or teenager; someone who is not a woman yet.

give.definition: If you give a speech, you talk to a group of people.
give.sentence: Give me that book, please; I want to read it.

glad.definition: If you are glad about something, you are happy about it.
glad.sentence: I'm glad to hear you're feeling better.

glance.definition: To look for a short moment (at something).

glass.definition: Glass is a transparent solid and is usually clear. Windows and eyeglasses are made from it, as well as drinking glasses.
glass.sentence: Through the window glass I could see the trees bend in the wind, but I was warm indoors.

global.definition: If something is global it includes the whole world.
global.sentence: The weather is changing, and this is not just in one or two places. The change is global.

go.definition: If you go, you move in space, especially to or through a place.
go.sentence: I go to the seashore every summer.

goal.definition: A goal is something you want to do or be able to do.
goal.sentence: I want to go to university and this will help me achieve that goal.

god.definition: The gods come from several powerful supernatural beings, according to some religions.
god.sentence: Wayne Gretzky is sometimes called a god of ice hockey.

gold.definition: Gold is a metal, which can be used to make coins and rings. It costs a lot of money to buy. Its symbol is Au on the periodic table and its atomic number is 79.
gold.sentence: I keep my gold in a safe.

golden.definition: If something is golden it is made from gold.
golden.sentence: Her hair was a golden blond.

golf.definition: Golf is a game where a person uses a club to try to hit a ball into a hole with the fewest strokes.
golf.sentence: He played golf with a friend.

good.definition: When you are good, you do the right things. That is, you do things that are kind or helpful. You do not do things that hurt people or are not honest.
good.sentence: He is a good person and would never steal.

govern.definition: If x governs y, x controls y through laws or other rules.
govern.sentence: Most transitive verbs govern the accusative case in German.

government.definition: A government is a group of people who make the laws and control a country or other place.

governor.definition: A governor is a person who leads a place like a state or territory.
governor.sentence: The king appointed a new governor for the province.

grab.definition: If you grab something, you quickly reach out and take it in your hand.

grade.definition: A grade is a letter or number that you use to show how good something is. Usually, teachers use it to show how good a student's test or assignment is.
grade.sentence: Our restaurant uses only the highest grade of meat.

gradually.definition: If something happens gradually, it happens in a gradual manner.
gradually.sentence: The everyday lifes of the citizens gradually went back to normal after the earthquake.

graduate.definition: If you graduate you get a degree or diploma from a school or university.

grain.definition: A grain is a seed that people eat, such as wheat, rice, corn, etc.
grain.sentence: One grain of salt is almost too small to see.

grammar.definition: The branch of linguistics that deals with syntax and morphology (and sometimes also deals with semantics)

grand.definition: If something is grand, it's large and impressive.
grand.sentence: As she got out of the car, she saw that the house was very grand.

grandmother.definition: Someone's grandmother is the mother of one of their parents.
grandmother.sentence: The mother of my mother is Jane Smith. Jane Smith is my grandmother.

grant.definition: If you grant something to something, you give it to them, usually formally.
grant.sentence: Yes, I'll grant you that the data is old, but I still think it's useful.

grass.definition: Grass is a green, leafy plant that often covers the ground.
grass.sentence: We haven't got much rain, and the grass on the lawn is turning brown.

grateful.definition: If you are grateful for or about something, you want to say, "thank you" because of it.
grateful.sentence: I'm very grateful for your kindness during this difficult time.

gray.definition: One of the colors people can see. It is halfway between black and white.
gray.sentence: I like the darker color of gray.

great.definition: A great object or event is very big and large in scale.
great.sentence: A great storm is approaching our shores.

greatly.definition: If something changes greatly, the change is very big.
greatly.sentence: Expenses greatly exceeded revenues this year.

green.definition: One of the colors people can see:
green.sentence: The ball rolled across the green and into the bunker.

greet.definition: If you greet someone or something, you meet them and say, "hello" or welcome them somehow.

grin.definition: A grin is a small smile, or a smile where you can see the teeth.

ground.definition: The ground is what someone stands or sits on when they are outside.
ground.sentence: I ran out of the house and fell on the ground.

group.definition: When more than 2 things or people are together, they make a group.
group.sentence: A group of people went into the building.

grow.definition: When things grow they get bigger or change in other ways over time.
grow.sentence: Every day I grow better and better.

growth.definition: The act of growing (getting bigger); an increase in size, number, value, or strength.
growth.sentence: I'm pleased with the growth in value of our house in the years after we bought it.

guarantee.definition: A guarantee is a formal promise that a product will be fixed or replaced or money will be repaid if it breaks or doesn't work.
guarantee.sentence: The phone is covered by a six-month guarantee on parts and labour.

guard.definition: A guard is a person or a group of people who watch something and try to stop anything bad from happening to it.
guard.sentence: After leaving the police he worked as a security guard at an airport.

guess.definition: If you guess at something, you try to imagine what it might be, but you don't know the answer.
guess.sentence: I guess she is angry at me for standing her up.

guest.definition: A guest is a person who you welcome into your house, your office, etc.

guideline.definition: A guideline is a formal suggestion about how something should be done, but it is not a rule.

guilty.definition: If you are guilty of something, you did it. This is usually for doing a bad thing.

guitar.definition: A guitar is a stringed musical instrument, usually with six strings, but sometimes more. It is used to play many kinds of music, including classical, rock, jazz, and bluegrass.

guy.definition: A guy is a boy or a man.
guy.sentence: So, I walk in and there's this woman talking to this guy.
